planMarkdown:
Bot: Production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for points wallet and transaction dashboard

Summary:
Build a Telegram bot with an attached Mini App that lets users open a secure dashboard, view their points balance, inspect transaction history, and understand how points were earned or spent. The bot acts as the conversational entry point and notification layer, while the Mini App provides the richer wallet experience.

The system runs as a single Node.js service using ESM and grammY. MongoDB stores user profiles, wallet balances, transaction ledger records, Mini App sessions, and audit metadata. The design prioritizes ledger correctness, Telegram identity verification, idempotent transaction processing, clear user support flows, and simple operational deployment.

Product goals:
1) Core user experience
Users should be able to start the bot, register automatically from their Telegram identity, and open a Mini App dashboard from an inline button or menu button. The dashboard shows current points balance, total earned, total spent or deducted, and recent transaction activity.

2) Wallet and ledger
The wallet should be points-based, not a financial banking wallet unless additional compliance work is done. Every balance change must be backed by an immutable transaction record. The displayed balance can be stored for fast reads, but the transaction ledger remains the source of truth for audits and reconciliation.

3) Transaction history
Users need a clear chronological history including transaction type, amount, status, timestamp, source, description, and optional reference ID. Typical transaction types include signup bonus, campaign reward, referral reward, manual adjustment, redemption, reversal, and expiry.

4) Dashboard clarity
The Mini App should provide a simple dashboard with balance card, summary stats, transaction list, filters by type and status, and transaction detail view. It should be mobile-first because most users will access it inside Telegram.

5) Admin and support readiness
Production operation requires admin visibility into users, balances, and transaction records. At minimum, define protected admin bot commands or an internal admin view for searching users, issuing adjustments, reversing mistakes, and exporting audit information. All admin mutations should create audit entries.

6) Trust and safety
The system should prevent fake Mini App requests by verifying Telegram Mini App init data. It should prevent duplicate rewards using idempotency keys. It should expose clear support commands so users can report missing points or confusing transactions.

High-level architecture:
1) Single service boundary
Run one Node.js ESM service that contains the grammY bot, the Mini App backend API, and shared domain services. The process handles Telegram updates, serves API endpoints for the Mini App, connects to MongoDB, and performs periodic maintenance tasks if needed.

2) Main components
The grammY bot layer handles commands, onboarding, inline keyboards, Mini App launch buttons, notifications, and admin commands. It should be thin and delegate wallet logic to domain services.

The Mini App frontend is a small web interface opened inside Telegram. It calls the backend API to retrieve user profile, balance, summary, and paginated transactions. It must send Telegram Mini App init data with API requests so the backend can authenticate the Telegram user.

The backend API validates Mini App init data, resolves the Telegram user, enforces authorization, and returns wallet data. It should expose only user-scoped endpoints unless the requester is an admin.

The wallet domain service owns all balance mutations. It creates ledger transactions, updates cached wallet balances, enforces idempotency, validates allowed transaction types, and records audit metadata.

The notification service sends Telegram messages for important events such as points credited, redemption completed, large adjustment, failed operation, or support response.

3) Data consistency approach
Use MongoDB transactions if available in the current MongoDB setup, especially when writing a wallet balance update and ledger transaction together. If multi-document transactions are not available, design writes to be idempotent and reconcileable by storing unique transaction keys and using atomic updates on wallet balance documents.

4) Ledger-first model
Do not directly change a user balance without creating a transaction. A transaction should have a stable lifecycle such as pending, completed, failed, reversed, or expired. Only completed transactions should affect the available balance unless the product later introduces reserved or pending balances.

5) Authentication and authorization
For bot messages, Telegram update context identifies the user. For Mini App requests, verify Telegram init data on every authenticated request or issue a short-lived server session after verification. Admin actions should be restricted by a configured list of Telegram user IDs stored in environment configuration or MongoDB.

6) Error handling
User-facing errors should be friendly and actionable. Internal errors should be logged with correlation IDs and enough context to investigate, without exposing secrets or raw tokens. Wallet mutations should return deterministic responses for duplicated idempotency keys.

7) Observability
Track structured logs for command usage, Mini App authentication failures, wallet mutation attempts, transaction creation, balance reconciliation, and admin operations. Add health checks for process liveness and MongoDB connectivity.

Data model:
1) User
Stores Telegram identity and account metadata. Suggested fields: internal user ID, telegramUserId, username, firstName, lastName, languageCode, createdAt, updatedAt, lastSeenAt, status, roles, referralCode, referredByUserId, and notification preferences.

2) Wallet
Stores the current cached balance for one user. Suggested fields: userId, availablePoints, lifetimeEarnedPoints, lifetimeSpentPoints, lifetimeAdjustedPoints, transactionCount, version, createdAt, updatedAt. The version field helps with optimistic concurrency and audit clarity.

3) WalletTransaction
Stores every balance-affecting or attempted wallet event. Suggested fields: transactionId, userId, type, direction, amount, status, balanceBefore, balanceAfter, description, source, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, metadata, createdAt, completedAt, reversedTransactionId, createdBy, and audit reason.

Transaction direction should be credit, debit, or neutral. Amount should be a positive integer. Status determines whether it affects balance. Use unique indexes on idempotencyKey where present, and indexes on userId plus createdAt for fast history pagination.

4) MiniAppSession or AuthRecord
Optional but useful if the backend exchanges verified Telegram init data for a short-lived session. Suggested fields: sessionId, userId, telegramUserId, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, ipHash, userAgentHash, and revokedAt. If not using sessions, validate init data per request and skip this collection.

5) RewardRule
Optional if points earning is campaign-driven. Suggested fields: ruleId, name, trigger, pointsAmount, startAt, endAt, maxClaimsPerUser, globalMaxClaims, status, metadata, and createdBy. This allows future expansion without hardcoding every campaign.

6) RewardClaim
Optional but recommended for preventing repeated earning. Suggested fields: claimId, userId, ruleId, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, status, transactionId, createdAt. This separates reward eligibility from wallet ledger mutation.

7) AuditLog
Stores sensitive administrative and system events. Suggested fields: auditId, actorUserId, actorRole, action, targetUserId, targetEntityType, targetEntityId, beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot, reason, createdAt, requestId.

8) SupportTicket
Optional for production support. Suggested fields: ticketId, userId, category, message, relatedTransactionId, status, adminNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt.

Key flows:
1) First-time onboarding
User sends /start. The bot creates or updates the user record from Telegram profile data, creates a wallet if missing, and replies with a short explanation plus a button to open the Mini App dashboard. If referral or campaign parameters are present in the start payload, the bot validates eligibility and creates the appropriate reward claim and wallet transaction.

2) Open dashboard
User taps the Mini App button. The Mini App loads inside Telegram and receives Telegram init data. The backend verifies the init data, resolves the user, updates lastSeenAt, and returns profile, balance summary, and recent transactions. The frontend displays a compact wallet dashboard and lets the user paginate through history.

3) Award points
A reward trigger occurs, such as signup, referral, campaign action, or admin adjustment. The wallet service receives a command with userId, transaction type, amount, source, sourceRef, and idempotencyKey. It checks that the idempotency key has not already been processed, creates a completed credit transaction, updates the wallet cached balance atomically, and optionally sends a Telegram notification.

4) Spend or redeem points
User initiates a redemption from the Mini App or bot. The backend verifies the user and checks available balance. It creates a debit transaction only if sufficient points exist. For external fulfillment, use pending status first, then mark completed or failed after fulfillment result. Failed debits should not reduce the final available balance.

5) Transaction history pagination
Mini App requests transactions with cursor-based pagination using createdAt and transactionId. The backend returns a stable ordered page, minimal metadata for the list, and a detail endpoint for full transaction information. This avoids slow offset pagination as history grows.

6) Reversal and correction
Admins should not delete transactions. To correct an error, create a reversing transaction that references the original transaction. The wallet service updates balance accordingly and marks the original transaction as reversed if appropriate. The audit log captures who performed the reversal and why.

7) Balance reconciliation
A scheduled or admin-triggered reconciliation recalculates balances from completed ledger transactions and compares them to wallet cached balances. Any mismatch creates an alert log and optionally a correction workflow. This is important for production confidence.

8) Support request
User sends /support or uses a dashboard support action. The bot collects a short message and optional transaction reference. The system creates a support ticket and confirms receipt. Admins can review and respond through protected commands or an internal support workflow.

Tech stack:
1) Runtime and language
Use a single Node.js service written with ESM. Keep domain logic framework-independent so bot handlers, Mini App API routes, and admin operations all call the same wallet service.

2) Telegram bot
Use grammY for Telegram bot handling. Read the bot token from the TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN environment variable. Use grammY middleware for logging, error boundaries, session-like conversational state if needed, and command routing.

3) Persistence
Use MongoDB, which is already integrated, for users, wallets, transactions, reward claims, sessions, audit logs, and support tickets. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable only for optional short-lived process-local caches, such as temporary rate limit counters or pending support prompts, and should not be used for critical wallet state.

4) Mini App backend
Serve authenticated API endpoints from the same Node.js process. Verify Telegram Mini App init data before returning user wallet information. Keep API responses small and mobile-friendly.

5) Mini App frontend
Build a mobile-first Telegram Mini App dashboard that uses Telegram Web App capabilities for launch context and user identity handoff. It should rely on the backend for all trusted wallet data and never compute authoritative balances on the client.

6) Storage for files
If support attachments, export files, or user-facing images are needed, use generic object storage or simple filesystem storage. Do not store large binary files directly in MongoDB unless they are very small and operationally acceptable.

7) Configuration
Use environment variables for the Telegram bot token, MongoDB connection settings, Mini App URL, admin Telegram user IDs, public base URL, log level, and security-related timeouts.

8) Deployment
Deploy as a Node.js server in the cloud. The service may receive Telegram updates through webhook mode for production, with long polling reserved for local development or simple staging environments.

Non-functional requirements:
1) Security
Verify Telegram Mini App init data for dashboard API access. Never trust user IDs sent directly by the client. Protect admin commands with explicit allowlists and role checks. Avoid logging secrets, tokens, raw init data, or sensitive personal information.

2) Wallet correctness
All balance changes must go through the wallet service. Use idempotency keys for reward and redemption operations. Store immutable ledger entries and prefer reversal transactions over edits or deletion. Validate that amounts are positive integers and that debits cannot make available balance negative.

3) Reliability
Use centralized error handling for grammY updates and API requests. Bot command failures should not crash the process. Wallet writes should be atomic where possible and safe to retry. Startup should fail fast if required configuration such as TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN or MongoDB settings is missing.

4) Performance
Index users by telegramUserId, wallets by userId, transactions by userId and createdAt, and idempotencyKey for duplicate prevention. Use cursor pagination for transaction history. Cache only non-critical derived data in memory, and tolerate cache loss on process restart.

5) Privacy
Collect only profile information needed for the bot experience. Provide a clear support path for account or data questions. Keep audit logs limited to operationally necessary details.

6) Abuse prevention
Add basic rate limits for commands, Mini App API calls, support ticket creation, and reward claiming. Use MongoDB-backed uniqueness for claims and idempotency so process restarts do not allow repeated rewards.

7) Maintainability
Separate modules by responsibility: bot handlers, Mini App API, wallet service, reward service, user service, admin service, persistence repositories, and shared validation. Keep business rules in services, not in UI handlers.

8) Operations
Provide health checks, structured logs, and admin diagnostics for user lookup and transaction inspection. Define a manual incident process for pausing reward rules, disabling redemptions, and reconciling balances if inconsistencies are detected.

Bot commands:
• /start — Creates or refreshes the user account, initializes the wallet if needed, explains the points wallet, and shows a button to open the Mini App dashboard. (usage: /start or /start referralpayload) [user]
• /wallet — Shows the current points balance and a quick link to open the Mini App dashboard for full details. (usage: /wallet) [user]
• /history — Shows the most recent wallet transactions in chat and offers a button to view the full transaction history in the Mini App. (usage: /history) [user]
• /dashboard — Returns the Mini App launch button for the wallet dashboard. (usage: /dashboard) [user]
• /help — Explains available commands, how points are earned, where to see history, and how to contact support. (usage: /help) [user]
• /support — Starts a support request flow for missing points, incorrect transactions, redemption questions, or account issues. (usage: /support) [user]
• /adminuser — Admin-only command to look up a user by Telegram user ID or username and view profile, wallet summary, and recent activity. (usage: /adminuser 123456789) [admin]
• /adminadjust — Admin-only command to issue a credit or debit adjustment with a required reason. The operation creates a ledger transaction and audit log entry. (usage: /adminadjust 123456789 credit 500 reason) [admin]
• /adminreverse — Admin-only command to reverse a specific transaction by creating an opposite ledger transaction linked to the original. (usage: /adminreverse transactionid reason) [admin]
• /adminreconcile — Admin-only command to run or request a balance reconciliation for one user or for the system, depending on permissions and operational policy. (usage: /adminreconcile 123456789) [admin]

DOCS.md.content:
# Points Wallet Bot

Points Wallet is a Telegram Mini App bot that creates a wallet profile for each Telegram user and shows a private dashboard with points balance and transaction history.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes your wallet profile and sends a button to open the Mini App dashboard.
- /help — Explains how to use the bot and where to view balance and transaction history.

## Mini App

The Mini App is hosted by the same Node.js service at `/app`.

The bot builds the dashboard button from the configured base URL and appends `/app` in code. Use a base URL only, for example:

`APP_BASE_URL=https://your-service.onrender.com`

Do not include `/app` in the environment value.

For CookMyBots or Render deployments, `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` may be injected automatically. `APP_BASE_URL` is also supported and has a local development fallback of `http://localhost:4000`.

## Environment variables

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required. Telegram bot token from BotFather.
- MONGODB_URI — Required. MongoDB connection string used for wallet persistence.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional. Public base URL for the Mini App button. Defaults safely for local development.
- PUBLIC_BASE_URL — Optional. CookMyBots-managed public base URL alias.
- PORT — Optional. HTTP server port. Defaults to 4000.

The service logs only boolean environment sanity checks, never secrets or connection strings.

## Database collections

- users — Telegram identity, username, names, status, createdAt, updatedAt, and lastSeenAt.
- wallets — Current cached points balance, total earned, total spent, transaction count, createdAt, and updatedAt.
- transactions — Chronological wallet ledger records with user id, type, amount, description, status, createdAt, and updatedAt.

Indexes are created for Telegram user lookup, wallet lookup, and transaction history. The app never creates an index on `_id`.

## Mini App API

All private wallet endpoints require Telegram WebApp init data in the `x-telegram-init-data` header. The backend verifies the signature with the bot token before returning private data.

- GET /api/wallet/summary — Returns the current user's profile, points balance, totals, and latest activity.
- GET /api/wallet/transactions — Returns recent transactions for the verified user.
- GET /health — Returns a safe health status with boolean config checks.

## Local development

1. Install root dependencies:
   `npm install`

2. Install and build the web app:
   `npm run install:webapp`
   `npm run build:webapp`

3. Configure `.env` from `.env.sample`.

4. Start the single service:
   `npm start`

The service listens on `PORT` or 4000 and serves the Mini App at `/app`.

## Deployment

Set at least `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `MONGODB_URI`. Set `APP_BASE_URL` only if the platform does not provide a public base URL automatically.

Use the root build command:
`npm run build`

Use the start command:
`npm start`

The bot uses long polling with webhook clearing before polling starts, so it is safe for first deploys and brief deploy overlap.

A production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for viewing points balances and transaction history.

## Features

- Telegram bot built with grammY.
- React, Vite, and Tailwind Mini App served at `/app`.
- Single Node.js service for bot, API, and web app hosting.
- MongoDB-backed users, wallets, and transactions.
- Telegram WebApp init data verification before private wallet data is returned.
- Mobile-first dashboard with loading, empty, and error states.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes the wallet profile and opens the dashboard.
- /help — Shows usage help.

## Environment

Copy `.env.sample` and set:

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required Telegram bot token.
- MONGODB_URI — Required MongoDB connection string.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional public base URL for the Mini App. Use a base URL only, not `/app`.
- PORT — Optional server port. Defaults to 4000.

## Run locally

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run install:webapp`
3. `npm run build:webapp`
4. `npm start`

Open `http://localhost:4000/app` for the web app shell. Private wallet data loads only inside Telegram with valid WebApp init data.

## Architecture

- `src/index.js` boots config, MongoDB, Express, and Telegram polling.
- `src/bot.js` creates the grammY bot and registers command modules.
- `src/commands` contains public bot commands.
- `src/services/wallet.js` owns wallet profile reads and writes.
- `src/server.js` serves `/app` and authenticated wallet API endpoints.
- `webapp` contains the React Mini App.

## Database

Collections:

- users
- wallets
- transactions

The wallet starts at 0 points. No fake user data is seeded.

## Deployment

Use:

- Build command: `npm run build`
- Start command: `npm start`

The service clears any Telegram webhook and starts long polling with retry/backoff. Logs include safe startup checks and database operation failures without printing secrets.

Bot: Production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for points wallet and transaction dashboard

Summary:
Build a Telegram bot with an attached Mini App that lets users open a secure dashboard, view their points balance, inspect transaction history, and understand how points were earned or spent. The bot acts as the conversational entry point and notification layer, while the Mini App provides the richer wallet experience.

The system runs as a single Node.js service using ESM and grammY. MongoDB stores user profiles, wallet balances, transaction ledger records, Mini App sessions, and audit metadata. The design prioritizes ledger correctness, Telegram identity verification, idempotent transaction processing, clear user support flows, and simple operational deployment.

Product goals:
1) Core user experience
Users should be able to start the bot, register automatically from their Telegram identity, and open a Mini App dashboard from an inline button or menu button. The dashboard shows current points balance, total earned, total spent or deducted, and recent transaction activity.

2) Wallet and ledger
The wallet should be points-based, not a financial banking wallet unless additional compliance work is done. Every balance change must be backed by an immutable transaction record. The displayed balance can be stored for fast reads, but the transaction ledger remains the source of truth for audits and reconciliation.

3) Transaction history
Users need a clear chronological history including transaction type, amount, status, timestamp, source, description, and optional reference ID. Typical transaction types include signup bonus, campaign reward, referral reward, manual adjustment, redemption, reversal, and expiry.

4) Dashboard clarity
The Mini App should provide a simple dashboard with balance card, summary stats, transaction list, filters by type and status, and transaction detail view. It should be mobile-first because most users will access it inside Telegram.

5) Admin and support readiness
Production operation requires admin visibility into users, balances, and transaction records. At minimum, define protected admin bot commands or an internal admin view for searching users, issuing adjustments, reversing mistakes, and exporting audit information. All admin mutations should create audit entries.

6) Trust and safety
The system should prevent fake Mini App requests by verifying Telegram Mini App init data. It should prevent duplicate rewards using idempotency keys. It should expose clear support commands so users can report missing points or confusing transactions.

High-level architecture:
1) Single service boundary
Run one Node.js ESM service that contains the grammY bot, the Mini App backend API, and shared domain services. The process handles Telegram updates, serves API endpoints for the Mini App, connects to MongoDB, and performs periodic maintenance tasks if needed.

2) Main components
The grammY bot layer handles commands, onboarding, inline keyboards, Mini App launch buttons, notifications, and admin commands. It should be thin and delegate wallet logic to domain services.

The Mini App frontend is a small web interface opened inside Telegram. It calls the backend API to retrieve user profile, balance, summary, and paginated transactions. It must send Telegram Mini App init data with API requests so the backend can authenticate the Telegram user.

The backend API validates Mini App init data, resolves the Telegram user, enforces authorization, and returns wallet data. It should expose only user-scoped endpoints unless the requester is an admin.

The wallet domain service owns all balance mutations. It creates ledger transactions, updates cached wallet balances, enforces idempotency, validates allowed transaction types, and records audit metadata.

The notification service sends Telegram messages for important events such as points credited, redemption completed, large adjustment, failed operation, or support response.

3) Data consistency approach
Use MongoDB transactions if available in the current MongoDB setup, especially when writing a wallet balance update and ledger transaction together. If multi-document transactions are not available, design writes to be idempotent and reconcileable by storing unique transaction keys and using atomic updates on wallet balance documents.

4) Ledger-first model
Do not directly change a user balance without creating a transaction. A transaction should have a stable lifecycle such as pending, completed, failed, reversed, or expired. Only completed transactions should affect the available balance unless the product later introduces reserved or pending balances.

5) Authentication and authorization
For bot messages, Telegram update context identifies the user. For Mini App requests, verify Telegram init data on every authenticated request or issue a short-lived server session after verification. Admin actions should be restricted by a configured list of Telegram user IDs stored in environment configuration or MongoDB.

6) Error handling
User-facing errors should be friendly and actionable. Internal errors should be logged with correlation IDs and enough context to investigate, without exposing secrets or raw tokens. Wallet mutations should return deterministic responses for duplicated idempotency keys.

7) Observability
Track structured logs for command usage, Mini App authentication failures, wallet mutation attempts, transaction creation, balance reconciliation, and admin operations. Add health checks for process liveness and MongoDB connectivity.

Data model:
1) User
Stores Telegram identity and account metadata. Suggested fields: internal user ID, telegramUserId, username, firstName, lastName, languageCode, createdAt, updatedAt, lastSeenAt, status, roles, referralCode, referredByUserId, and notification preferences.

2) Wallet
Stores the current cached balance for one user. Suggested fields: userId, availablePoints, lifetimeEarnedPoints, lifetimeSpentPoints, lifetimeAdjustedPoints, transactionCount, version, createdAt, updatedAt. The version field helps with optimistic concurrency and audit clarity.

3) WalletTransaction
Stores every balance-affecting or attempted wallet event. Suggested fields: transactionId, userId, type, direction, amount, status, balanceBefore, balanceAfter, description, source, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, metadata, createdAt, completedAt, reversedTransactionId, createdBy, and audit reason.

Transaction direction should be credit, debit, or neutral. Amount should be a positive integer. Status determines whether it affects balance. Use unique indexes on idempotencyKey where present, and indexes on userId plus createdAt for fast history pagination.

4) MiniAppSession or AuthRecord
Optional but useful if the backend exchanges verified Telegram init data for a short-lived session. Suggested fields: sessionId, userId, telegramUserId, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, ipHash, userAgentHash, and revokedAt. If not using sessions, validate init data per request and skip this collection.

5) RewardRule
Optional if points earning is campaign-driven. Suggested fields: ruleId, name, trigger, pointsAmount, startAt, endAt, maxClaimsPerUser, globalMaxClaims, status, metadata, and createdBy. This allows future expansion without hardcoding every campaign.

6) RewardClaim
Optional but recommended for preventing repeated earning. Suggested fields: claimId, userId, ruleId, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, status, transactionId, createdAt. This separates reward eligibility from wallet ledger mutation.

7) AuditLog
Stores sensitive administrative and system events. Suggested fields: auditId, actorUserId, actorRole, action, targetUserId, targetEntityType, targetEntityId, beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot, reason, createdAt, requestId.

8) SupportTicket
Optional for production support. Suggested fields: ticketId, userId, category, message, relatedTransactionId, status, adminNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt.

Key flows:
1) First-time onboarding
User sends /start. The bot creates or updates the user record from Telegram profile data, creates a wallet if missing, and replies with a short explanation plus a button to open the Mini App dashboard. If referral or campaign parameters are present in the start payload, the bot validates eligibility and creates the appropriate reward claim and wallet transaction.

2) Open dashboard
User taps the Mini App button. The Mini App loads inside Telegram and receives Telegram init data. The backend verifies the init data, resolves the user, updates lastSeenAt, and returns profile, balance summary, and recent transactions. The frontend displays a compact wallet dashboard and lets the user paginate through history.

3) Award points
A reward trigger occurs, such as signup, referral, campaign action, or admin adjustment. The wallet service receives a command with userId, transaction type, amount, source, sourceRef, and idempotencyKey. It checks that the idempotency key has not already been processed, creates a completed credit transaction, updates the wallet cached balance atomically, and optionally sends a Telegram notification.

4) Spend or redeem points
User initiates a redemption from the Mini App or bot. The backend verifies the user and checks available balance. It creates a debit transaction only if sufficient points exist. For external fulfillment, use pending status first, then mark completed or failed after fulfillment result. Failed debits should not reduce the final available balance.

5) Transaction history pagination
Mini App requests transactions with cursor-based pagination using createdAt and transactionId. The backend returns a stable ordered page, minimal metadata for the list, and a detail endpoint for full transaction information. This avoids slow offset pagination as history grows.

6) Reversal and correction
Admins should not delete transactions. To correct an error, create a reversing transaction that references the original transaction. The wallet service updates balance accordingly and marks the original transaction as reversed if appropriate. The audit log captures who performed the reversal and why.

7) Balance reconciliation
A scheduled or admin-triggered reconciliation recalculates balances from completed ledger transactions and compares them to wallet cached balances. Any mismatch creates an alert log and optionally a correction workflow. This is important for production confidence.

8) Support request
User sends /support or uses a dashboard support action. The bot collects a short message and optional transaction reference. The system creates a support ticket and confirms receipt. Admins can review and respond through protected commands or an internal support workflow.

Tech stack:
1) Runtime and language
Use a single Node.js service written with ESM. Keep domain logic framework-independent so bot handlers, Mini App API routes, and admin operations all call the same wallet service.

2) Telegram bot
Use grammY for Telegram bot handling. Read the bot token from the TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN environment variable. Use grammY middleware for logging, error boundaries, session-like conversational state if needed, and command routing.

3) Persistence
Use MongoDB, which is already integrated, for users, wallets, transactions, reward claims, sessions, audit logs, and support tickets. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable only for optional short-lived process-local caches, such as temporary rate limit counters or pending support prompts, and should not be used for critical wallet state.

4) Mini App backend
Serve authenticated API endpoints from the same Node.js process. Verify Telegram Mini App init data before returning user wallet information. Keep API responses small and mobile-friendly.

5) Mini App frontend
Build a mobile-first Telegram Mini App dashboard that uses Telegram Web App capabilities for launch context and user identity handoff. It should rely on the backend for all trusted wallet data and never compute authoritative balances on the client.

6) Storage for files
If support attachments, export files, or user-facing images are needed, use generic object storage or simple filesystem storage. Do not store large binary files directly in MongoDB unless they are very small and operationally acceptable.

7) Configuration
Use environment variables for the Telegram bot token, MongoDB connection settings, Mini App URL, admin Telegram user IDs, public base URL, log level, and security-related timeouts.

8) Deployment
Deploy as a Node.js server in the cloud. The service may receive Telegram updates through webhook mode for production, with long polling reserved for local development or simple staging environments.

Non-functional requirements:
1) Security
Verify Telegram Mini App init data for dashboard API access. Never trust user IDs sent directly by the client. Protect admin commands with explicit allowlists and role checks. Avoid logging secrets, tokens, raw init data, or sensitive personal information.

2) Wallet correctness
All balance changes must go through the wallet service. Use idempotency keys for reward and redemption operations. Store immutable ledger entries and prefer reversal transactions over edits or deletion. Validate that amounts are positive integers and that debits cannot make available balance negative.

3) Reliability
Use centralized error handling for grammY updates and API requests. Bot command failures should not crash the process. Wallet writes should be atomic where possible and safe to retry. Startup should fail fast if required configuration such as TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN or MongoDB settings is missing.

4) Performance
Index users by telegramUserId, wallets by userId, transactions by userId and createdAt, and idempotencyKey for duplicate prevention. Use cursor pagination for transaction history. Cache only non-critical derived data in memory, and tolerate cache loss on process restart.

5) Privacy
Collect only profile information needed for the bot experience. Provide a clear support path for account or data questions. Keep audit logs limited to operationally necessary details.

6) Abuse prevention
Add basic rate limits for commands, Mini App API calls, support ticket creation, and reward claiming. Use MongoDB-backed uniqueness for claims and idempotency so process restarts do not allow repeated rewards.

7) Maintainability
Separate modules by responsibility: bot handlers, Mini App API, wallet service, reward service, user service, admin service, persistence repositories, and shared validation. Keep business rules in services, not in UI handlers.

8) Operations
Provide health checks, structured logs, and admin diagnostics for user lookup and transaction inspection. Define a manual incident process for pausing reward rules, disabling redemptions, and reconciling balances if inconsistencies are detected.

Bot commands:
• /start — Creates or refreshes the user account, initializes the wallet if needed, explains the points wallet, and shows a button to open the Mini App dashboard. (usage: /start or /start referralpayload) [user]
• /wallet — Shows the current points balance and a quick link to open the Mini App dashboard for full details. (usage: /wallet) [user]
• /history — Shows the most recent wallet transactions in chat and offers a button to view the full transaction history in the Mini App. (usage: /history) [user]
• /dashboard — Returns the Mini App launch button for the wallet dashboard. (usage: /dashboard) [user]
• /help — Explains available commands, how points are earned, where to see history, and how to contact support. (usage: /help) [user]
• /support — Starts a support request flow for missing points, incorrect transactions, redemption questions, or account issues. (usage: /support) [user]
• /adminuser — Admin-only command to look up a user by Telegram user ID or username and view profile, wallet summary, and recent activity. (usage: /adminuser 123456789) [admin]
• /adminadjust — Admin-only command to issue a credit or debit adjustment with a required reason. The operation creates a ledger transaction and audit log entry. (usage: /adminadjust 123456789 credit 500 reason) [admin]
• /adminreverse — Admin-only command to reverse a specific transaction by creating an opposite ledger transaction linked to the original. (usage: /adminreverse transactionid reason) [admin]
• /adminreconcile — Admin-only command to run or request a balance reconciliation for one user or for the system, depending on permissions and operational policy. (usage: /adminreconcile 123456789) [admin]

# Points Wallet Bot

Points Wallet is a Telegram Mini App bot that creates a wallet profile for each Telegram user and shows a private dashboard with points balance and transaction history.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes your wallet profile and sends a button to open the Mini App dashboard.
- /help — Explains how to use the bot and where to view balance and transaction history.

## Mini App

The Mini App is hosted by the same Node.js service at `/app`.

The bot builds the dashboard button from the configured base URL and appends `/app` in code. Use a base URL only, for example:

`APP_BASE_URL=https://your-service.onrender.com`

Do not include `/app` in the environment value.

For CookMyBots or Render deployments, `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` may be injected automatically. `APP_BASE_URL` is also supported and has a local development fallback of `http://localhost:4000`.

## Environment variables

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required. Telegram bot token from BotFather.
- MONGODB_URI — Required. MongoDB connection string used for wallet persistence.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional. Public base URL for the Mini App button. Defaults safely for local development.
- PUBLIC_BASE_URL — Optional. CookMyBots-managed public base URL alias.
- PORT — Optional. HTTP server port. Defaults to 4000.

The service logs only boolean environment sanity checks, never secrets or connection strings.

## Database collections

- users — Telegram identity, username, names, status, createdAt, updatedAt, and lastSeenAt.
- wallets — Current cached points balance, total earned, total spent, transaction count, createdAt, and updatedAt.
- transactions — Chronological wallet ledger records with user id, type, amount, description, status, createdAt, and updatedAt.

Indexes are created for Telegram user lookup, wallet lookup, and transaction history. The app never creates an index on `_id`.

## Mini App API

All private wallet endpoints require Telegram WebApp init data in the `x-telegram-init-data` header. The backend verifies the signature with the bot token before returning private data.

- GET /api/wallet/summary — Returns the current user's profile, points balance, totals, and latest activity.
- GET /api/wallet/transactions — Returns recent transactions for the verified user.
- GET /health — Returns a safe health status with boolean config checks.

## Local development

1. Install root dependencies:
   `npm install`

2. Install and build the web app:
   `npm run install:webapp`
   `npm run build:webapp`

3. Configure `.env` from `.env.sample`.

4. Start the single service:
   `npm start`

The service listens on `PORT` or 4000 and serves the Mini App at `/app`.

## Deployment

Set at least `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `MONGODB_URI`. Set `APP_BASE_URL` only if the platform does not provide a public base URL automatically.

Use the root build command:
`npm run build`

Use the start command:
`npm start`

The bot uses long polling with webhook clearing before polling starts, so it is safe for first deploys and brief deploy overlap.

# Points Wallet Bot

A production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for viewing points balances and transaction history.

## Features

- Telegram bot built with grammY.
- React, Vite, and Tailwind Mini App served at `/app`.
- Single Node.js service for bot, API, and web app hosting.
- MongoDB-backed users, wallets, and transactions.
- Telegram WebApp init data verification before private wallet data is returned.
- Mobile-first dashboard with loading, empty, and error states.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes the wallet profile and opens the dashboard.
- /help — Shows usage help.

## Environment

Copy `.env.sample` and set:

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required Telegram bot token.
- MONGODB_URI — Required MongoDB connection string.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional public base URL for the Mini App. Use a base URL only, not `/app`.
- PORT — Optional server port. Defaults to 4000.

## Run locally

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run install:webapp`
3. `npm run build:webapp`
4. `npm start`

Open `http://localhost:4000/app` for the web app shell. Private wallet data loads only inside Telegram with valid WebApp init data.

## Architecture

- `src/index.js` boots config, MongoDB, Express, and Telegram polling.
- `src/bot.js` creates the grammY bot and registers command modules.
- `src/commands` contains public bot commands.
- `src/services/wallet.js` owns wallet profile reads and writes.
- `src/server.js` serves `/app` and authenticated wallet API endpoints.
- `webapp` contains the React Mini App.

## Database

Collections:

- users
- wallets
- transactions

The wallet starts at 0 points. No fake user data is seeded.

## Deployment

Use:

- Build command: `npm run build`
- Start command: `npm start`

The service clears any Telegram webhook and starts long polling with retry/backoff. Logs include safe startup checks and database operation failures without printing secrets.

Bot: Production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for points wallet and transaction dashboard

Summary:
Build a Telegram bot with an attached Mini App that lets users open a secure dashboard, view their points balance, inspect transaction history, and understand how points were earned or spent. The bot acts as the conversational entry point and notification layer, while the Mini App provides the richer wallet experience.

The system runs as a single Node.js service using ESM and grammY. MongoDB stores user profiles, wallet balances, transaction ledger records, Mini App sessions, and audit metadata. The design prioritizes ledger correctness, Telegram identity verification, idempotent transaction processing, clear user support flows, and simple operational deployment.

Product goals:
1) Core user experience
Users should be able to start the bot, register automatically from their Telegram identity, and open a Mini App dashboard from an inline button or menu button. The dashboard shows current points balance, total earned, total spent or deducted, and recent transaction activity.

2) Wallet and ledger
The wallet should be points-based, not a financial banking wallet unless additional compliance work is done. Every balance change must be backed by an immutable transaction record. The displayed balance can be stored for fast reads, but the transaction ledger remains the source of truth for audits and reconciliation.

3) Transaction history
Users need a clear chronological history including transaction type, amount, status, timestamp, source, description, and optional reference ID. Typical transaction types include signup bonus, campaign reward, referral reward, manual adjustment, redemption, reversal, and expiry.

4) Dashboard clarity
The Mini App should provide a simple dashboard with balance card, summary stats, transaction list, filters by type and status, and transaction detail view. It should be mobile-first because most users will access it inside Telegram.

5) Admin and support readiness
Production operation requires admin visibility into users, balances, and transaction records. At minimum, define protected admin bot commands or an internal admin view for searching users, issuing adjustments, reversing mistakes, and exporting audit information. All admin mutations should create audit entries.

6) Trust and safety
The system should prevent fake Mini App requests by verifying Telegram Mini App init data. It should prevent duplicate rewards using idempotency keys. It should expose clear support commands so users can report missing points or confusing transactions.

High-level architecture:
1) Single service boundary
Run one Node.js ESM service that contains the grammY bot, the Mini App backend API, and shared domain services. The process handles Telegram updates, serves API endpoints for the Mini App, connects to MongoDB, and performs periodic maintenance tasks if needed.

2) Main components
The grammY bot layer handles commands, onboarding, inline keyboards, Mini App launch buttons, notifications, and admin commands. It should be thin and delegate wallet logic to domain services.

The Mini App frontend is a small web interface opened inside Telegram. It calls the backend API to retrieve user profile, balance, summary, and paginated transactions. It must send Telegram Mini App init data with API requests so the backend can authenticate the Telegram user.

The backend API validates Mini App init data, resolves the Telegram user, enforces authorization, and returns wallet data. It should expose only user-scoped endpoints unless the requester is an admin.

The wallet domain service owns all balance mutations. It creates ledger transactions, updates cached wallet balances, enforces idempotency, validates allowed transaction types, and records audit metadata.

The notification service sends Telegram messages for important events such as points credited, redemption completed, large adjustment, failed operation, or support response.

3) Data consistency approach
Use MongoDB transactions if available in the current MongoDB setup, especially when writing a wallet balance update and ledger transaction together. If multi-document transactions are not available, design writes to be idempotent and reconcileable by storing unique transaction keys and using atomic updates on wallet balance documents.

4) Ledger-first model
Do not directly change a user balance without creating a transaction. A transaction should have a stable lifecycle such as pending, completed, failed, reversed, or expired. Only completed transactions should affect the available balance unless the product later introduces reserved or pending balances.

5) Authentication and authorization
For bot messages, Telegram update context identifies the user. For Mini App requests, verify Telegram init data on every authenticated request or issue a short-lived server session after verification. Admin actions should be restricted by a configured list of Telegram user IDs stored in environment configuration or MongoDB.

6) Error handling
User-facing errors should be friendly and actionable. Internal errors should be logged with correlation IDs and enough context to investigate, without exposing secrets or raw tokens. Wallet mutations should return deterministic responses for duplicated idempotency keys.

7) Observability
Track structured logs for command usage, Mini App authentication failures, wallet mutation attempts, transaction creation, balance reconciliation, and admin operations. Add health checks for process liveness and MongoDB connectivity.

Data model:
1) User
Stores Telegram identity and account metadata. Suggested fields: internal user ID, telegramUserId, username, firstName, lastName, languageCode, createdAt, updatedAt, lastSeenAt, status, roles, referralCode, referredByUserId, and notification preferences.

2) Wallet
Stores the current cached balance for one user. Suggested fields: userId, availablePoints, lifetimeEarnedPoints, lifetimeSpentPoints, lifetimeAdjustedPoints, transactionCount, version, createdAt, updatedAt. The version field helps with optimistic concurrency and audit clarity.

3) WalletTransaction
Stores every balance-affecting or attempted wallet event. Suggested fields: transactionId, userId, type, direction, amount, status, balanceBefore, balanceAfter, description, source, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, metadata, createdAt, completedAt, reversedTransactionId, createdBy, and audit reason.

Transaction direction should be credit, debit, or neutral. Amount should be a positive integer. Status determines whether it affects balance. Use unique indexes on idempotencyKey where present, and indexes on userId plus createdAt for fast history pagination.

4) MiniAppSession or AuthRecord
Optional but useful if the backend exchanges verified Telegram init data for a short-lived session. Suggested fields: sessionId, userId, telegramUserId, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, ipHash, userAgentHash, and revokedAt. If not using sessions, validate init data per request and skip this collection.

5) RewardRule
Optional if points earning is campaign-driven. Suggested fields: ruleId, name, trigger, pointsAmount, startAt, endAt, maxClaimsPerUser, globalMaxClaims, status, metadata, and createdBy. This allows future expansion without hardcoding every campaign.

6) RewardClaim
Optional but recommended for preventing repeated earning. Suggested fields: claimId, userId, ruleId, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, status, transactionId, createdAt. This separates reward eligibility from wallet ledger mutation.

7) AuditLog
Stores sensitive administrative and system events. Suggested fields: auditId, actorUserId, actorRole, action, targetUserId, targetEntityType, targetEntityId, beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot, reason, createdAt, requestId.

8) SupportTicket
Optional for production support. Suggested fields: ticketId, userId, category, message, relatedTransactionId, status, adminNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt.

Key flows:
1) First-time onboarding
User sends /start. The bot creates or updates the user record from Telegram profile data, creates a wallet if missing, and replies with a short explanation plus a button to open the Mini App dashboard. If referral or campaign parameters are present in the start payload, the bot validates eligibility and creates the appropriate reward claim and wallet transaction.

2) Open dashboard
User taps the Mini App button. The Mini App loads inside Telegram and receives Telegram init data. The backend verifies the init data, resolves the user, updates lastSeenAt, and returns profile, balance summary, and recent transactions. The frontend displays a compact wallet dashboard and lets the user paginate through history.

3) Award points
A reward trigger occurs, such as signup, referral, campaign action, or admin adjustment. The wallet service receives a command with userId, transaction type, amount, source, sourceRef, and idempotencyKey. It checks that the idempotency key has not already been processed, creates a completed credit transaction, updates the wallet cached balance atomically, and optionally sends a Telegram notification.

4) Spend or redeem points
User initiates a redemption from the Mini App or bot. The backend verifies the user and checks available balance. It creates a debit transaction only if sufficient points exist. For external fulfillment, use pending status first, then mark completed or failed after fulfillment result. Failed debits should not reduce the final available balance.

5) Transaction history pagination
Mini App requests transactions with cursor-based pagination using createdAt and transactionId. The backend returns a stable ordered page, minimal metadata for the list, and a detail endpoint for full transaction information. This avoids slow offset pagination as history grows.

6) Reversal and correction
Admins should not delete transactions. To correct an error, create a reversing transaction that references the original transaction. The wallet service updates balance accordingly and marks the original transaction as reversed if appropriate. The audit log captures who performed the reversal and why.

7) Balance reconciliation
A scheduled or admin-triggered reconciliation recalculates balances from completed ledger transactions and compares them to wallet cached balances. Any mismatch creates an alert log and optionally a correction workflow. This is important for production confidence.

8) Support request
User sends /support or uses a dashboard support action. The bot collects a short message and optional transaction reference. The system creates a support ticket and confirms receipt. Admins can review and respond through protected commands or an internal support workflow.

Tech stack:
1) Runtime and language
Use a single Node.js service written with ESM. Keep domain logic framework-independent so bot handlers, Mini App API routes, and admin operations all call the same wallet service.

2) Telegram bot
Use grammY for Telegram bot handling. Read the bot token from the TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN environment variable. Use grammY middleware for logging, error boundaries, session-like conversational state if needed, and command routing.

3) Persistence
Use MongoDB, which is already integrated, for users, wallets, transactions, reward claims, sessions, audit logs, and support tickets. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable only for optional short-lived process-local caches, such as temporary rate limit counters or pending support prompts, and should not be used for critical wallet state.

4) Mini App backend
Serve authenticated API endpoints from the same Node.js process. Verify Telegram Mini App init data before returning user wallet information. Keep API responses small and mobile-friendly.

5) Mini App frontend
Build a mobile-first Telegram Mini App dashboard that uses Telegram Web App capabilities for launch context and user identity handoff. It should rely on the backend for all trusted wallet data and never compute authoritative balances on the client.

6) Storage for files
If support attachments, export files, or user-facing images are needed, use generic object storage or simple filesystem storage. Do not store large binary files directly in MongoDB unless they are very small and operationally acceptable.

7) Configuration
Use environment variables for the Telegram bot token, MongoDB connection settings, Mini App URL, admin Telegram user IDs, public base URL, log level, and security-related timeouts.

8) Deployment
Deploy as a Node.js server in the cloud. The service may receive Telegram updates through webhook mode for production, with long polling reserved for local development or simple staging environments.

Non-functional requirements:
1) Security
Verify Telegram Mini App init data for dashboard API access. Never trust user IDs sent directly by the client. Protect admin commands with explicit allowlists and role checks. Avoid logging secrets, tokens, raw init data, or sensitive personal information.

2) Wallet correctness
All balance changes must go through the wallet service. Use idempotency keys for reward and redemption operations. Store immutable ledger entries and prefer reversal transactions over edits or deletion. Validate that amounts are positive integers and that debits cannot make available balance negative.

3) Reliability
Use centralized error handling for grammY updates and API requests. Bot command failures should not crash the process. Wallet writes should be atomic where possible and safe to retry. Startup should fail fast if required configuration such as TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN or MongoDB settings is missing.

4) Performance
Index users by telegramUserId, wallets by userId, transactions by userId and createdAt, and idempotencyKey for duplicate prevention. Use cursor pagination for transaction history. Cache only non-critical derived data in memory, and tolerate cache loss on process restart.

5) Privacy
Collect only profile information needed for the bot experience. Provide a clear support path for account or data questions. Keep audit logs limited to operationally necessary details.

6) Abuse prevention
Add basic rate limits for commands, Mini App API calls, support ticket creation, and reward claiming. Use MongoDB-backed uniqueness for claims and idempotency so process restarts do not allow repeated rewards.

7) Maintainability
Separate modules by responsibility: bot handlers, Mini App API, wallet service, reward service, user service, admin service, persistence repositories, and shared validation. Keep business rules in services, not in UI handlers.

8) Operations
Provide health checks, structured logs, and admin diagnostics for user lookup and transaction inspection. Define a manual incident process for pausing reward rules, disabling redemptions, and reconciling balances if inconsistencies are detected.

Bot commands:
• /start — Creates or refreshes the user account, initializes the wallet if needed, explains the points wallet, and shows a button to open the Mini App dashboard. (usage: /start or /start referralpayload) [user]
• /wallet — Shows the current points balance and a quick link to open the Mini App dashboard for full details. (usage: /wallet) [user]
• /history — Shows the most recent wallet transactions in chat and offers a button to view the full transaction history in the Mini App. (usage: /history) [user]
• /dashboard — Returns the Mini App launch button for the wallet dashboard. (usage: /dashboard) [user]
• /help — Explains available commands, how points are earned, where to see history, and how to contact support. (usage: /help) [user]
• /support — Starts a support request flow for missing points, incorrect transactions, redemption questions, or account issues. (usage: /support) [user]
• /adminuser — Admin-only command to look up a user by Telegram user ID or username and view profile, wallet summary, and recent activity. (usage: /adminuser 123456789) [admin]
• /adminadjust — Admin-only command to issue a credit or debit adjustment with a required reason. The operation creates a ledger transaction and audit log entry. (usage: /adminadjust 123456789 credit 500 reason) [admin]
• /adminreverse — Admin-only command to reverse a specific transaction by creating an opposite ledger transaction linked to the original. (usage: /adminreverse transactionid reason) [admin]
• /adminreconcile — Admin-only command to run or request a balance reconciliation for one user or for the system, depending on permissions and operational policy. (usage: /adminreconcile 123456789) [admin]

DOCS.md.content:
# Points Wallet Bot

Points Wallet is a Telegram Mini App bot that creates a wallet profile for each Telegram user and shows a private dashboard with points balance and transaction history.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes your wallet profile and sends a button to open the Mini App dashboard.
- /help — Explains how to use the bot and where to view balance and transaction history.

## Mini App

The Mini App is hosted by the same Node.js service at `/app`.

The bot builds the dashboard button from the configured base URL and appends `/app` in code. Use a base URL only, for example:

`APP_BASE_URL=https://your-service.onrender.com`

Do not include `/app` in the environment value.

For CookMyBots or Render deployments, `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` may be injected automatically. `APP_BASE_URL` is also supported and has a local development fallback of `http://localhost:4000`.

## Environment variables

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required. Telegram bot token from BotFather.
- MONGODB_URI — Required. MongoDB connection string used for wallet persistence.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional. Public base URL for the Mini App button. Defaults safely for local development.
- PUBLIC_BASE_URL — Optional. CookMyBots-managed public base URL alias.
- PORT — Optional. HTTP server port. Defaults to 4000.

The service logs only boolean environment sanity checks, never secrets or connection strings.

## Database collections

- users — Telegram identity, username, names, status, createdAt, updatedAt, and lastSeenAt.
- wallets — Current cached points balance, total earned, total spent, transaction count, createdAt, and updatedAt.
- transactions — Chronological wallet ledger records with user id, type, amount, description, status, createdAt, and updatedAt.

Indexes are created for Telegram user lookup, wallet lookup, and transaction history. The app never creates an index on `_id`.

## Mini App API

All private wallet endpoints require Telegram WebApp init data in the `x-telegram-init-data` header. The backend verifies the signature with the bot token before returning private data.

- GET /api/wallet/summary — Returns the current user's profile, points balance, totals, and latest activity.
- GET /api/wallet/transactions — Returns recent transactions for the verified user.
- GET /health — Returns a safe health status with boolean config checks.

## Local development

1. Install root dependencies:
   `npm install`

2. Install and build the web app:
   `npm run install:webapp`
   `npm run build:webapp`

3. Configure `.env` from `.env.sample`.

4. Start the single service:
   `npm start`

The service listens on `PORT` or 4000 and serves the Mini App at `/app`.

## Deployment

Set at least `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `MONGODB_URI`. Set `APP_BASE_URL` only if the platform does not provide a public base URL automatically.

Use the root build command:
`npm run build`

Use the start command:
`npm start`

The bot uses long polling with webhook clearing before polling starts, so it is safe for first deploys and brief deploy overlap.

# Points Wallet Bot

A production-ready Telegram Mini App bot for viewing points balances and transaction history.

## Features

- Telegram bot built with grammY.
- React, Vite, and Tailwind Mini App served at `/app`.
- Single Node.js service for bot, API, and web app hosting.
- MongoDB-backed users, wallets, and transactions.
- Telegram WebApp init data verification before private wallet data is returned.
- Mobile-first dashboard with loading, empty, and error states.

## Commands

- /start — Creates or refreshes the wallet profile and opens the dashboard.
- /help — Shows usage help.

## Environment

Copy `.env.sample` and set:

- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — Required Telegram bot token.
- MONGODB_URI — Required MongoDB connection string.
- APP_BASE_URL — Optional public base URL for the Mini App. Use a base URL only, not `/app`.
- PORT — Optional server port. Defaults to 4000.

## Run locally

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run install:webapp`
3. `npm run build:webapp`
4. `npm start`

Open `http://localhost:4000/app` for the web app shell. Private wallet data loads only inside Telegram with valid WebApp init data.

## Architecture

- `src/index.js` boots config, MongoDB, Express, and Telegram polling.
- `src/bot.js` creates the grammY bot and registers command modules.
- `src/commands` contains public bot commands.
- `src/services/wallet.js` owns wallet profile reads and writes.
- `src/server.js` serves `/app` and authenticated wallet API endpoints.
- `webapp` contains the React Mini App.

## Database

Collections:

- users
- wallets
- transactions

The wallet starts at 0 points. No fake user data is seeded.

## Deployment

Use:

- Build command: `npm run build`
- Start command: `npm start`

The service clears any Telegram webhook and starts long polling with retry/backoff. Logs include safe startup checks and database operation failures without printing secrets.

The notification service sends Telegram messages for important events such as points credited, redemption completed, large adjustment, failed operation, or support response.

3) Data consistency approach
Use MongoDB transactions if available in the current MongoDB setup, especially when writing a wallet balance update and ledger transaction together. If multi-document transactions are not available, design writes to be idempotent and reconcileable by storing unique transaction keys and using atomic updates on wallet balance documents.

4) Ledger-first model
Do not directly change a user balance without creating a transaction. A transaction should have a stable lifecycle such as pending, completed, failed, reversed, or expired. Only completed transactions should affect the available balance unless the product later introduces reserved or pending balances.

5) Authentication and authorization
For bot messages, Telegram update context identifies the user. For Mini App requests, verify Telegram init data on every authenticated request or issue a short-lived server session after verification. Admin actions should be restricted by a configured list of Telegram user IDs stored in environment configuration or MongoDB.

6) Error handling
User-facing errors should be friendly and actionable. Internal errors should be logged with correlation IDs and enough context to investigate, without exposing secrets or raw tokens. Wallet mutations should return deterministic responses for duplicated idempotency keys.

7) Observability
Track structured logs for command usage, Mini App authentication failures, wallet mutation attempts, transaction creation, balance reconciliation, and admin operations. Add health checks for process liveness and MongoDB connectivity.
planSections.dataModel:
1) User
Stores Telegram identity and account metadata. Suggested fields: internal user ID, telegramUserId, username, firstName, lastName, languageCode, createdAt, updatedAt, lastSeenAt, status, roles, referralCode, referredByUserId, and notification preferences.

2) Wallet
Stores the current cached balance for one user. Suggested fields: userId, availablePoints, lifetimeEarnedPoints, lifetimeSpentPoints, lifetimeAdjustedPoints, transactionCount, version, createdAt, updatedAt. The version field helps with optimistic concurrency and audit clarity.

3) WalletTransaction
Stores every balance-affecting or attempted wallet event. Suggested fields: transactionId, userId, type, direction, amount, status, balanceBefore, balanceAfter, description, source, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, metadata, createdAt, completedAt, reversedTransactionId, createdBy, and audit reason.

Transaction direction should be credit, debit, or neutral. Amount should be a positive integer. Status determines whether it affects balance. Use unique indexes on idempotencyKey where present, and indexes on userId plus createdAt for fast history pagination.

4) MiniAppSession or AuthRecord
Optional but useful if the backend exchanges verified Telegram init data for a short-lived session. Suggested fields: sessionId, userId, telegramUserId, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, ipHash, userAgentHash, and revokedAt. If not using sessions, validate init data per request and skip this collection.

5) RewardRule
Optional if points earning is campaign-driven. Suggested fields: ruleId, name, trigger, pointsAmount, startAt, endAt, maxClaimsPerUser, globalMaxClaims, status, metadata, and createdBy. This allows future expansion without hardcoding every campaign.

6) RewardClaim
Optional but recommended for preventing repeated earning. Suggested fields: claimId, userId, ruleId, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, status, transactionId, createdAt. This separates reward eligibility from wallet ledger mutation.

7) AuditLog
Stores sensitive administrative and system events. Suggested fields: auditId, actorUserId, actorRole, action, targetUserId, targetEntityType, targetEntityId, beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot, reason, createdAt, requestId.

8) SupportTicket
Optional for production support. Suggested fields: ticketId, userId, category, message, relatedTransactionId, status, adminNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt.
planSections.keyFlows:
1) First-time onboarding
User sends /start. The bot creates or updates the user record from Telegram profile data, creates a wallet if missing, and replies with a short explanation plus a button to open the Mini App dashboard. If referral or campaign parameters are present in the start payload, the bot validates eligibility and creates the appropriate reward claim and wallet transaction.

2) Open dashboard
User taps the Mini App button. The Mini App loads inside Telegram and receives Telegram init data. The backend verifies the init data, resolves the user, updates lastSeenAt, and returns profile, balance summary, and recent transactions. The frontend displays a compact wallet dashboard and lets the user paginate through history.

3) Award points
A reward trigger occurs, such as signup, referral, campaign action, or admin adjustment. The wallet service receives a command with userId, transaction type, amount, source, sourceRef, and idempotencyKey. It checks that the idempotency key has not already been processed, creates a completed credit transaction, updates the wallet cached balance atomically, and optionally sends a Telegram notification.

4) Spend or redeem points
User initiates a redemption from the Mini App or bot. The backend verifies the user and checks available balance. It creates a debit transaction only if sufficient points exist. For external fulfillment, use pending status first, then mark completed or failed after fulfillment result. Failed debits should not reduce the final available balance.

5) Transaction history pagination
Mini App requests transactions with cursor-based pagination using createdAt and transactionId. The backend returns a stable ordered page, minimal metadata for the list, and a detail endpoint for full transaction information. This avoids slow offset pagination as history grows.

6) Reversal and correction
Admins should not delete transactions. To correct an error, create a reversing transaction that references the original transaction. The wallet service updates balance accordingly and marks the original transaction as reversed if appropriate. The audit log captures who performed the reversal and why.

7) Balance reconciliation
A scheduled or admin-triggered reconciliation recalculates balances from completed ledger transactions and compares them to wallet cached balances. Any mismatch creates an alert log and optionally a correction workflow. This is important for production confidence.

8) Support request
User sends /support or uses a dashboard support action. The bot collects a short message and optional transaction reference. The system creates a support ticket and confirms receipt. Admins can review and respond through protected commands or an internal support workflow.
planSections.techStack:
1) Runtime and language
Use a single Node.js service written with ESM. Keep domain logic framework-independent so bot handlers, Mini App API routes, and admin operations all call the same wallet service.

2) Telegram bot
Use grammY for Telegram bot handling. Read the bot token from the TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN environment variable. Use grammY middleware for logging, error boundaries, session-like conversational state if needed, and command routing.

3) Persistence
Use MongoDB, which is already integrated, for users, wallets, transactions, reward claims, sessions, audit logs, and support tickets. Simple in-memory maps are acceptable only for optional short-lived process-local caches, such as temporary rate limit counters or pending support prompts, and should not be used for critical wallet state.

4) Mini App backend
Serve authenticated API endpoints from the same Node.js process. Verify Telegram Mini App init data before returning user wallet information. Keep API responses small and mobile-friendly.

5) Mini App frontend
Build a mobile-first Telegram Mini App dashboard that uses Telegram Web App capabilities for launch context and user identity handoff. It should rely on the backend for all trusted wallet data and never compute authoritative balances on the client.

6) Storage for files
If support attachments, export files, or user-facing images are needed, use generic object storage or simple filesystem storage. Do not store large binary files directly in MongoDB unless they are very small and operationally acceptable.

7) Configuration
Use environment variables for the Telegram bot token, MongoDB connection settings, Mini App URL, admin Telegram user IDs, public base URL, log level, and security-related timeouts.

8) Deployment
Deploy as a Node.js server in the cloud. The service may receive Telegram updates through webhook mode for production, with long polling reserved for local development or simple staging environments.
planSections.nonFunctional:
1) Security
Verify Telegram Mini App init data for dashboard API access. Never trust user IDs sent directly by the client. Protect admin commands with explicit allowlists and role checks. Avoid logging secrets, tokens, raw init data, or sensitive personal information.

2) Wallet correctness
All balance changes must go through the wallet service. Use idempotency keys for reward and redemption operations. Store immutable ledger entries and prefer reversal transactions over edits or deletion. Validate that amounts are positive integers and that debits cannot make available balance negative.

3) Reliability
Use centralized error handling for grammY updates and API requests. Bot command failures should not crash the process. Wallet writes should be atomic where possible and safe to retry. Startup should fail fast if required configuration such as TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN or MongoDB settings is missing.

4) Performance
Index users by telegramUserId, wallets by userId, transactions by userId and createdAt, and idempotencyKey for duplicate prevention. Use cursor pagination for transaction history. Cache only non-critical derived data in memory, and tolerate cache loss on process restart.

5) Privacy
Collect only profile information needed for the bot experience. Provide a clear support path for account or data questions. Keep audit logs limited to operationally necessary details.

6) Abuse prevention
Add basic rate limits for commands, Mini App API calls, support ticket creation, and reward claiming. Use MongoDB-backed uniqueness for claims and idempotency so process restarts do not allow repeated rewards.

7) Maintainability
Separate modules by responsibility: bot handlers, Mini App API, wallet service, reward service, user service, admin service, persistence repositories, and shared validation. Keep business rules in services, not in UI handlers.

8) Operations
Provide health checks, structured logs, and admin diagnostics for user lookup and transaction inspection. Define a manual incident process for pausing reward rules, disabling redemptions, and reconciling balances if inconsistencies are detected.
